title: Paediatric Hip and Knee Conditions: DDH, Perthes Disease, SCFE and Osgood-Schlatter
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Limping child is the key presentation for hip conditions. SCFE and Perthes often present with knee or thigh pain, not hip pain. Always examine the hip in a child with knee pain.
working: Paediatric Hip and Knee Conditions: DDH, Perthes Disease, SCFE and Osgood-Schlatter

differentials.name: Septic arthritis
differentials.next: Very painful, held flexed, any movement painful

qa: Why examine the hip in a child with knee pain? Hip conditions such as SCFE and Perthes often refer pain to the knee.
What is obligatory external rotation? The thigh rotates outward when the hip is flexed: a sign of SCFE.
How do you separate septic arthritis from transient synovitis? Fever, refusal to bear weight and a very unwell child suggest septic arthritis: emergency.
Does Osgood-Schlatter need complete rest? No. Load management and strengthening.
Which age group typically gets Perthes? About 4 to 8 years.

redFlags.Finding: Fever, unwell, refusing to bear weight, severe pain on any hip movement
Adolescent with hip, thigh or knee pain and obligatory external rotation; unable to bear weight
Night pain, weight loss, bruising, pallor

manualNotes: DDH: managed by orthopaedics (harness, casting, surgery); physiotherapy for range and gross motor development after treatment.
Perthes: maintain hip range (especially abduction and internal rotation), strength, low-impact activity (swimming, cycling), activity modification as advised by orthopaedics.

SCFE: surgical fixation; physiotherapy after surgery for gait, strength and gradual return to sport per surgeon. Osgood-Schlatter and Sever disease: education (self-limiting, settles with growth plate closure); load management (reduce jumping volume, not complete rest); quadriceps or calf strengthening and flexibility; pain-guided return; heel raise insert for Sever. Pain up to about 3 to 4/10 during activity that settles by the next day is acceptable [Ref – to verify].
